title: Harvard to Offer Executive Education Courses in Hyderabad from December
excerpt: Telangana CM A. Revanth Reddy announced Thursday that Harvard executive education programmes will launch in Hyderabad in December 2026, with MIT and Purdue offshore campuses also in the works as the state pushes to become a global knowledge hub.
body:
• Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy announced Thursday that Harvard University will offer executive education courses in Hyderabad starting December 2026, part of a bid to build the state into a "global knowledge hub."
  • The announcement came during a meeting with a 30-member delegation of UK universities and business schools at the MCR HRD Institute, including Lord Karan Bilimoria and British Council officials.
  • Processes for offshore campuses of MIT and Purdue in Hyderabad are already underway, and Telangana is exploring partnerships with Harvard, University of London, Virginia Tech and Northeastern University across executive education, dual degrees and faculty training.
  • Reddy himself completed a six-day leadership programme at Harvard's Kennedy School of Government in January 2026, and he invited global education leaders to the Invest Telangana Global Summit in December.

Harvard University will offer executive education courses in Hyderabad starting this December, Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy announced Thursday, a move the state government says will help turn Telangana into a global knowledge hub.

Reddy made the announcement during a meeting with a 30-member delegation of UK universities and business schools at the MCR HRD Institute in Hyderabad. The delegation included UK House of Lords member Lord Karan Bilimoria, British Council representative Janaka Pushpanathan, Chartered Association of Business Schools CEO Flora Hamilton and officials of the British Deputy High Commission, according to reports by The News Trust and Telugu360.

The Chief Minister said the Telangana government was taking rapid strides toward transforming the state into a "global knowledge hub," and assured the delegation of state support for universities establishing offshore campuses in Hyderabad.

More Partnerships in the Pipeline

Reddy said the process for setting up offshore campuses of MIT and Purdue in Hyderabad was already underway, according to an official release. Partnerships under discussion with Harvard, MIT, University of London, Virginia Tech and Northeastern University span executive education, dual-degree programmes, faculty training and research.

He briefed the delegation on the proposed Bharat Future City — a 30,000-acre net-zero greenfield smart city — where the government plans an education hub alongside global companies and research institutions. The Chief Minister said the presence of international institutions would help local universities collaborate on research and industry partnerships while giving Telangana students and faculty greater access to international academic exposure, according to Telugu360.

Reddy also invited UK universities and education leaders to the Invest Telangana Global Summit 2026, scheduled for December, which the state plans to develop on the lines of the World Economic Forum's annual meeting in Davos.

"Make Telangana a place where the world comes to learn, innovate and invest. $1 Trillion by 2034 | $3 Trillion by 2047. That's our target."

— A. Revanth Reddy, Chief Minister of Telangana, on X

Context & Background

The announcement has a personal thread: earlier this year, Reddy enrolled in a six-day "Leadership in the 21st Century" programme at Harvard University's Kennedy School of Government, with orientation beginning January 25, 2026. According to the Chief Minister's office, he is the first sitting chief minister in India to enrol in an Ivy League programme, joining a cohort of students from over 20 countries. The move drew criticism from the BJP's state unit at the time, which questioned the timing and cost.

Telangana has been pitching Hyderabad as a destination for global education institutions for months. The state already hosts the Indian School of Business and a dense concentration of IT and pharma companies, giving it an existing base of working professionals who are the natural audience for executive education. Reddy has said the world is looking to Hyderabad "not just for investments and business, but for knowledge, skills, talent, innovation, and the ideas that will shape the future."

Impact & Analysis

Executive education from a brand like Harvard carries a different weight than a degree programme: it targets senior working professionals, entrepreneurs and government officials, and is typically delivered in short, intensive formats. If Harvard follows through with in-person courses in Hyderabad, it would place India among a small group of countries where the university delivers its executive programmes outside Cambridge — and it would sharpen competition among Indian metros to host global education brands. The MIT and Purdue offshore-campus processes, if completed, would go further, giving Hyderabad a cluster of American research institutions with physical footprints.

Details that matter — which Harvard school's programmes, the admission criteria, and the fee structure — have not yet been announced. The December launch date coincides with the Invest Telangana Global Summit, suggesting the state wants the programme live as a showcase for its education ambitions.

Diaspora Angle

For Indian diaspora professionals, especially the large Hyderabad-origin cohort working in tech and management roles in the United States, Harvard executive courses delivered in India open a new channel: mid-career credentials from a globally recognised brand without a Cambridge price tag, and a reason to spend time in the city during career breaks. Dual-degree programmes and faculty training could also draw diaspora academics into teaching and research partnerships with Hyderabad institutions.

What's Next

The programmes are slated to begin in December 2026. Watch for the course catalogue and fee details, which will determine whether the offering is aimed at Hyderabad's corporate leadership or a broader national audience. The December Global Summit will be the next checkpoint for the MIT and Purdue campus plans.
